waivers.reason: Both `if (canResumeLive)` at MirrorAnnotationStage.kt:321 and `dimmed = frozen != null && marks.isNotEmpty()` at :286 live inside a @Composable with no Compose UI-test harness in this repo; mutating either back to the pre-fix shape (independently re-verified by me, not just read) leaves all 235 tests green. The underlying predicates ARE mutation-proven pure (`resumeLiveIsNotOfferedWhileTheSessionIsLost`, ScrimGateTest), and the dropped state is covered by a light/dark @Preview pair — but the WIRING between predicate and composable render is unproven by any assertion that can fail. This is accepted as a known ceiling for this spec rather than fixed, because fixing it needs either a new UI-test harness or hoisting both gates into the pure projection layer (DiscoveryErrorProjection-style) — both are real follow-on work, not a same-spec fix. T-16-coverage-honest.md recommends the hoist as the cheaper option for reflection.

waivers.item: Hard-wedge adb daemon recovery is unsolved (T-8's wedged-daemon finding)
waivers.reason: adb kill-server works by asking the daemon to exit over its own socket; a daemon that cannot answer `adb devices` cannot answer that either, so the ladder's step 3 (KillServer then StartServer) classifies and escalates on a hard wedge correctly every time but cannot clear it. Confirmed on real hardware (SIGSTOP approximation): ~24s/cycle, falls back to PollFailed with the real reason, never loops silently. No AC or SC requires full recovery from a hard wedge — FR-36's own prose overclaims this slightly ('the only sequence that recovers a wedged daemon'), but the tested/shipped contract is escalate-correctly-then-report, which is what ships. Escalating to killing the daemon pid directly was considered and explicitly rejected as a bigger decision than this spec should make unilaterally.
waivers.acceptedBy: plan/execution (ai-proposed; discovered during T-8, not decided by a human this run, but blocks no AC/SC text as written)

One correction to my own briefing, found by reading code rather than notes: execution/GAP-fr37-immediate-repoll.md says 'T-retry is NOT WRITTEN' and TEST-NAME-MAP.md repeats it — both predate commit 34b87d5. I found a CONFLATED Channel-based refreshDiscovery() in DeviceRepositoryImpl.observeDiscovery's own poll loop (a `withTimeoutOrNull(DiscoveryPollMs) { refreshRequests.receive() }` race), exactly the fix GAP-fr37-immediate-repoll.md's own recommendation describes, with two new mutation-killed tests ('a refresh request cuts the poll interval short', 'a refresh requested between polls is not lost') added in 34b87d5. AC-28/SC-12 was re-verified as reachable, not merely reasoned about: errorCard()'s picker-guard now only yields to an open picker for DiscoveryModel.Found (ToolMissing and PollFailed never did, per the pre-existing T-14 guard), and a new mutation-proven test (theAmbiguityCardIsReachableOnceThePickerIsClosed) asserts the card appears once the picker is closed with 2+ usable devices present. Hard open gaps that remain genuinely open, confirmed by me rather than taken on faith: the NFR-6 composable-level gate (Resume Live withdrawal, scrim dimming) has zero commonTest coverage of its wiring — I re-read both call sites and the structure is unchanged from T-16-coverage-honest.md's description; T-11's pre-fix RED run for AC-54/T2 is unrecoverable (the pre-fix tree no longer exists; a permanent mutation guard (M8) stands in its place and is honestly distinguished from a pre-fix transcript in TEST-NAME-MAP.md and GAPS-for-later-waves.md); hard-wedge daemon recovery is a discovered, not decided, limitation.

AF-11 (restartAdb()/adbPathChosen() discard their use case's Result/Failure silently, unlike boot()'s .onFailure{} pattern) remains unfixed. It is a warn-severity finding, not one of the four error-severity items the two fix commits targeted, and it does not unsatisfy any AC's literal text — recorded here for the next wave rather than as a verdict blocker.

Trace-ID collisions (SC-10/SC-11 vs F-4, FR-23 vs app-shell-window-layout, FR-24 vs android-device-discovery-mirroring) and the 195-test baseline off-by-one correction are pre-existing, already-documented, and not defects — carried forward unchanged per plan.json's own instruction not to renumber.

changelog.summary: F-3 wires all four of F-2's previously-unrendered typed discovery-failure states into shipped ErrorCard/CommandBlock/SourceListRow kit components, fixes a reproduced-on-hardware adb cold-daemon livelock with a hardware-verified budgeted escalation ladder, and fixes a real NFR-6 violation in merged F-4 code (the only affordance offered on an involuntary disconnect destroyed staged annotations). Two post-audit fix commits (34b87d5, 94e442a) closed all four error-severity and one warn-severity audit finding; I independently re-ran the builds/tests rather than trusting the commit messages or the audit, and found one of the execution notes (T-retry 'not written') was itself stale — the fix had already landed. 235 tests pass (0 failures), 0 of the 195-test baseline lost, and :presentation-feature-mirror:build / :data-repository-impl:build are genuinely green including iosSimulatorArm64Test execution (not just compilation) on a fresh --rerun-tasks run. Open, honestly-recorded limitations remain: the NFR-6 composable-level gate has no regression guard reachable without a new UI-test harness or a projection hoist; a hard-wedged adb daemon is correctly detected and reported but cannot be forcibly cleared; T-11's pre-fix RED run for AC-54 could not be captured (the pre-fix tree was lost to an agent's mid-session death) and a permanent mutation guard stands in its place, honestly distinguished from a transcript; and T-18's physical USB unplug/replug verification was explicitly skipped by direct operator decision, the only human-made call in this run.
